title: Ties
summary: Join two notes into one long sound, even across a bar line.

hook.text: Some notes are too long for one [[bar|bar]]. A singer can hold a note over the [[bar-line|bar line]], but you cannot write a note on top of a line. Press play and listen for the note that carries on into the next [[bar|bar]]. How would you write it?

explore.text: Your turn. Count 1, 2, 3, 4 with the clicks. Tap on each note. Where a curved line joins two notes, tap only the first one and hold through the second. Keep counting.
explore.goal: Tap each joined pair once only: 3, 3, 2 and 4 taps in the four [[bar|bars]].

cards.text: That curved line is a [[tie|tie]]. It joins two notes of the same [[pitch|pitch]] into one long sound: play the first and hold through the second. Add the lengths: a [[minim|minim]] tied to a [[crotchet|crotchet]] lasts 2 + 1 = 3 beats.

A tie can also cross a [[bar-line|bar line]]. A note cannot sit on the line, so write it in two parts, one at the end of a [[bar|bar]] and one at the start of the next, joined by a tie. A dot can only add half; a tie can add any note.

A tie also keeps the middle of a 4/4 [[bar|bar]] clear. A sound that starts on beat 2 and lasts 1½ beats is a [[crotchet|crotchet]] tied to one [[quaver|quaver]], so you can still see where beat 3 begins.

alternative.text: Think of pushing a swing. A note is one push. A tie says: do not push again, let the swing carry on through the next note. A [[minim|minim]] tied to a [[crotchet|crotchet]] is one push and 3 beats of swinging.

questions.prompt: Both clips start on the same note. In one, a [[tie|tie]] holds that note for 3 beats. Which clip?

options.reason: In clip B the first note lasts 2 beats and a new note starts on beat 3. The tied note in clip A carries on through beat 3.

questions.prompt: One sound starts on beat 2 and lasts 1½ beats. Which [[bar|bar]] writes it the standard way?

options.reason: That dotted [[crotchet|crotchet]] starts on beat 2 and runs over the middle of the [[bar|bar]], hiding beat 3. A tie splits it so beat 3 shows.
There is no tie here, so the second [[crotchet|crotchet]] lasts only 1 beat. The sound stops when beat 3 arrives, so it is not 1½ beats long.

questions.prompt: What must two tied notes have in common?

options.reason: Tied notes can have different lengths: a [[minim|minim]] can be tied to a [[crotchet|crotchet]]. What they share is the same [[pitch|pitch]].
A tie can cross a [[bar-line|bar line]], so the two notes can sit in different [[bar|bars]]. What they share is the same [[pitch|pitch]].

questions.prompt: One sound starts on beat 2 and lasts to the end of the [[bar|bar]]. Which [[bar|bar]] writes it the standard way?
questions.hint: Which [[bar|bar]] keeps the sound going from beat 2 to the end, and still lets you see beat 3?

options.reason: That dotted [[minim|minim]] starts on beat 2 and runs over the middle of the [[bar|bar]], hiding beat 3. Tie a [[crotchet|crotchet]] to a [[minim|minim]] instead.
That is four separate [[crotchet|crotchets]], so nothing is held. The sound should start on beat 2 and carry on to the end.

questions.prompt: Put these tied sounds in order, shortest first.
questions.hint: Add the two beats together for each pair, then sort the totals.

points: A [[tie|tie]] is a curved line joining two notes of the same [[pitch|pitch]]. Play the first and hold through the second: their lengths add up.
A tie can cross a [[bar-line|bar line]]. Split the note in two, one part each side of the line, and join the parts with a tie.
In 4/4 use a tie to keep the middle of the [[bar|bar]] clear. A sound from beat 2 that lasts 1½ beats is a [[crotchet|crotchet]] tied to one [[quaver|quaver]].
